source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Working in essentially the same way as a standard ACE inhibitor medication, without any additional distinct mechanism of its own beyond that single effect","B":"Inhibiting neprilysin (which breaks down beneficial natriuretic peptides) while also blocking the angiotensin II receptor, providing complementary benefits for heart failure","C":"Working mainly by blocking beta receptors and calcium channels in cardiac tissue, rather than through its actual dual neprilysin and receptor-blocking mechanism","D":"Having fairly little effect on the renin-angiotensin system at all, despite being classified within that broader cardiovascular medication category"}}
source_row.rationale: Sacubitril/valsartan combines neprilysin inhibition (which increases levels of beneficial natriuretic peptides that would otherwise be broken down) with angiotensin receptor blockade, providing a dual, complementary mechanism shown to reduce mortality and hospitalization in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
source_row.source_name: PMC — Angiotensin Receptor Neprilysin Inhibition Mechanism
